items.title: DeFranco Buddy — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: We had Clark Terry, Wardell Gray, and myself on the front lines. And he had Jimmy Lewis played bass

ctx.x: So when you were playing with that group what was it? Was it a septet, or octet?

Yeah, it was septet. We had Clark Terry, Wardell Gray, and myself on the front lines. And he had Jimmy Lewis played bass, Gus Johnson was a great drummer; he played drums, and Bill, of course, piano. And then one night we were playing and Freddie Green came in, and he was a notorious player with Bill Basie for years.

items.title: Buddy DeFranco interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, April 13, 1996
items.q: Bill Basie and Jimmy Lewis played bass and Gus Johnson played drums.

ctx.x: It started out Clark Terry and Bobby Graf from St. Louis, a tenor player, myself on front line, Bill Basie and Jimmy Lewis played bass and Gus Johnson played drums. And shortly after that, Freddie Green joined and that was fantastic. It really made that group.
You had to have Freddie, right?

items.title: Jimmy Lewis interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, November 16, 1995
items.q: me on bass and like we used Bud DeFranco playing tenor.

ctx.x: Is this when Basie had the small group?
Yes, the small group. We had Wardell Gray, Clark Terry, Gus Johnson on drums, Freddie Green on guitar, me on bass and like we used Bud DeFranco playing tenor.
Can I read something that Joe Williams said about that group?
